title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 3 and 4.
This question paper consists of 5 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

questions.prompt: What is a trade union?
questions.memo:
✓ An organisation of workers (1)
✓ formed to protect and improve their wages, working conditions and rights (1)

questions.prompt: Which union was founded by Clements Kadalie in 1919? (abbreviation)
What does the CCMA do?
According to the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, what is the maximum number of ordinary working hours per week?
The right to strike includes the right to damage property.
Discuss TWO advantages and TWO disadvantages of trade unions for the economy.
questions.memo:
Advantages (1 each): better wages increase spending; safer workplaces; stability through bargaining
Disadvantages (1 each): strikes reduce production; job losses from high wage demands; violence scares investors

sections.title: QUESTION 3: The General Ledger and Trial Balance

questions.prompt: The total of the Sales column in the Debtors Journal is posted to:

questions.prompt: What does the abbreviation 'b/d' stand for when balancing an account?
Classify each account and show its normal balance.
Creditors control had a credit balance of R7 400 on 1 May. Credit purchases in May were R15 600 and payments to creditors were R13 200. What is the balance on 31 May?

A learner's trial balance shows debit balances of R59 350 and credit balances of R60 250. She finds that Stationery of R450 was placed in the credit column. Explain why correcting this error makes the trial balance balance.
questions.memo:
✓ Stationery is an expense, so it has a debit balance (1)
✓ moving it to the debit column: debits R59 350 + R450 = R59 800 (1)
✓ credits R60 250 − R450 = R59 800, so the totals now agree (1)
